name: eCoin pivotal study
aliases: Leadless tibial nerve stimulator pivotal study
question: What proportion of adults with refractory urgency urinary incontinence responded to implanted eCoin tibial nerve stimulation after 48 weeks of therapy?

arms.label: eCoin leadless implantable tibial nerve stimulator

design.population: 137 adults with refractory urgency urinary incontinence were enrolled at 15 US centers; 133 received an implant and 132 entered the published intention-to-treat analysis.
design.description: Prospective, multicenter, open-label, single-arm pivotal device study
design.locator: PubMed abstract, Materials and methods and Results

verdictNote: The observed responder rate was 68% at 48 weeks in this single-arm study.
takeaway: In a single-arm pivotal study, implanted eCoin leadless tibial nerve stimulation was associated with at least 50% fewer urgency incontinence episodes in 68% of the published intention-to-treat cohort at 48 weeks after activation.

reports.label: 48-week pivotal report
reports.citation: Rogers A, Bragg S, Ferrante K, et al. "Pivotal Study of Leadless Tibial Nerve Stimulation with eCoin® for Urgency Urinary Incontinence: An Open-Label, Single Arm Trial." *J Urol.* 2021;206(2):399-408. doi:10.1097/JU.0000000000001733
reports.followUp: 48 weeks after activation for efficacy; 52 weeks after implantation for device-related adverse events
reports.followUpLocator: PubMed abstract, Materials and methods and Results

results.measure: At least 50% fewer urgency urinary incontinence episodes at 48 weeks after activation; published intention-to-treat population (n=132)
results.note: The accessible abstract does not state the prespecified performance goal or test result.

harms.label: Device-related adverse events through 52 weeks after implantation
harms.note: The FDA physician labeling uses a different device-related event count; see notes.md.

harms.locator: FDA physician labeling P200036D, p32, Table 2
harms.note: This broader event category is from FDA labeling, not the journal abstract.

harms.label: Serious device- or procedure-related adverse events, FDA labeling analysis
harms.locator: FDA physician labeling P200036D, p32, Tables 2-3
harms.note: Three infections and one contact dermatitis led to explantation.

delivery.label: Implant location and treatment delivery
delivery.value: eCoin was implanted in the lower leg above the fascia over the tibial nerve and delivered automated stimulation sessions.

delivery.label: Procedure setting and activation
delivery.value: Implantation was primarily in office settings under local anesthesia; activation followed a 4-week healing period, then 30-minute sessions every 3 days for 18 weeks and every 4 days thereafter.
delivery.locator: FDA physician labeling P200036D, pp25-26, Study Design
delivery.note: FDA labeling describes the same pivotal cohort.

reports.citation: Lucente V, Giusto L, MacDiarmid S. "Two-year Pivotal Study Analysis of the Safety and Efficacy of Implantable Tibial Nerve Stimulation With eCoin® for Urgency Urinary Incontinence." *Urology.* 2024;194:17-23. doi:10.1016/j.urology.2024.07.046

results.measure: At least 50% fewer urgency urinary incontinence episodes at 96 weeks; 72 completed the evaluation, but the abstract does not give the analysis denominator

results.endpoint: At least 75% fewer urgency urinary incontinence episodes
